text:
I am extremely disappointed with this McDonald’s location.

I placed a mobile pickup order and picked it up without checking it. When I got home, I was shocked to see that my muffin was completely burnt. The muffin was black and overcooked, and the food was not edible at all. It was so badly burnt that I had no choice but to throw it away. This is unacceptable. If you are serving food to customers, at least make sure it is properly cooked and not burnt to this level.

This is not the first issue I have had here. A few days ago, I placed a mobile order before 10:30 AM. I arrived at 10:38 AM, and they had canceled my order without any proper explanation. When I asked about it, the cashier was very rude and did not even try to explain the reason. There was no apology, no effort to help, and no basic customer service.

The quality of food and the way customers are treated at this location is unacceptable. I strongly recommend everyone to avoid this location. This kind of careless food preparation and rude behavior towards customers should not be tolerated.

Very disappointed
author: preetham adluri

text: This is a failed McDonald's trying to hold on in a failed city. Seattle was once a great city, and now it is just a failure. A big failure. This McDonald's has coos standing at the corner watching everyone. And violent people nearby yelling at the pavement washers, while the police just stand there doing nothing. And the dining area is shut down--looks nice but no entry. In fact the front door is barricaded and you can't enter it. Instead you stand at the door barricade and hope someone shows up to take your order, and just wait and wait. Eventually they take your order and eventually you get your food. But the dining area is shut down, maybe to avoid liability for the high drug use and violence in the area? Maybe dining area had druggies doing drugs in that area? Regardless, if you go here be aware of what you are walking in to. Do not feel safe, keep both eyes open, watch your 6. Stay alert, stay alive.  Reminds me much of downtown Minneapolis. Oh, and the same meal that costs me $17 in Virginia, costs me $28 at this place. Wow!!.  Thanks to the new minimum wage laws
author: Jeff W

text: This place is dangerous to go to.  I'm not joking.  Because of the area and its unfortunate location, there is always a group of drug addicts openly smoking right infront of the store.  They have the dinning room shut down so you have to stand out there with them and order at a window.  I used to go several times a week, but had to stop after I was assaulted one time, and last time I was there a lady who was falling asleep while standing infront of the store woke up long enough to accuse me of "looking at her too long" and pulled out a tazer and attempted to taze me.  I hadn't even noticed her until she said something.   The employees at the store are to busy either goofing off inside, ignoring a line of people to visit with each other, or they are too busy talking to the same people that make it so dangerous to be there to actually take an order.   I cannot understate this enough, avoid this place at all cost. For your own safety and well-being.
author: Nick Barrera

text: I had an extremely frustrating experience at this location. I ordered a Happy Meal specifically for the Crocs toy + other stuff, but they forgot the sauces for both my order and the group ahead of me. Although I tried to be understanding, I later realized I also received the wrong toy. When I returned, I learned they were out of the Crocs toy, which anyone would have expected to at least get notified at pickup. I didn't ask for a refund since it was inexpensive, and I wanted to leave quickly given this location is known for being very unsafe. Additionally, they forgot the apple slices, which I discovered only after I got home. Overall, it was a disappointing visit, and I recommend checking your order carefully or avoiding this place altogether.
author: Yo-Lei Chen

text: The staff were a bit short with my wife and kids but you can see that the homeless situation around the location is challenging and wears on the employees. I have never seen an urban McDonalds  where you can’t go in due to the risk of the surrounding environment. I believe the front facing of the location needs to reimagined if there is no access to the public and the city need to partner with the businesses for safety concerns. The smell of urine alone and pressure to give people money on the street, made us leave after we paid for some food. There were some food trucks in front of Nordstrom rack that had a cleaner and safer feel for a quick snack

text:
This place is peak Seattle: dirty, depressing, and surrounded by the kind of characters that make you question if society was a bad idea. You can’t even go inside—probably because it’s safer that way—so you’re stuck waiting on the sidewalk, watching a live demo of what happens when a city gives up.

I didn’t eat here, and I never will. I just felt obligated to leave this PSA for any poor tourist who still thinks Seattle has “charm.” Do yourself a favor—hand your wallet to the nearest guy screaming at traffic, stab yourself with a rusty fork, and skip the wait. Same experience, less hassle.
author: Lucas Svaren

text:
First of all, this is just a sketchy place
So many crackheads and is just terrible.
The employees were over worked and overwhelmed. I honestly felt bad for them. As well as the homeless which were swarming all around the place. Smokers galore. If u want to get high on the amount of drugs here, feel free. Overall not good at all just a bad place. Don’t take you kids here unless you want them a traumatic experience. Also very expensive. Manager argued with me about the 14 dollar big Mack. Wasn’t even a meal. They were “out of stock” Never come here.

text: Pretty sad that people can't come inside this McDonald's location anymore. 3rd Avenue has always been "animated" but I never had any issues. Just keep aware what's going on around you and don't leave your bag/purse open. My sister had her bag stolen at a bus stop at this location years ago because she wasn't hanging onto it well and it was pretty open. I don't mind walking in this area but I wouldn't stand around ordering from this McDonald's now. Must have gotten BAD cause this McDonald's was open to the public to go in for YEARS.
author: M W

text: This is by far the worst fast food in Seattle. The worst McDonalds I've EVER been to. Felt incredibly unsafe while there because of the drug use right next to the pick-up window. They don't even let you inside the lobby to pick up your order. Customer service is unacceptable. I hope the management can turn this place around soon. I'm sure it's hard to keep good employees at this location. They need security all hours they are open patrolling the pick-up windows to keep the drug use and crime away.
author: Tennessee Oiler

text:
Food was mediocre, even in comparison to other McDonald’s, but most of all, the McDonald’s was heavily barricaded, there was no dine in spot, and the environment outside was extremely bad because of the homelessness.

The service was also bad and they were spending time greeting to friends who for some reason got to sit inside the otherwise  deserted restaurant while we could only order from the outside. It took very long to get our food and it was overall not a pleasant experience.
author: James Wang

text: Expensive, compromised quality, and full of other impatient and rude customers. No wonder the people working here are so moody. Considering what they must be getting paid and the hours they work, I have to respect their brusk attitudes, but I have a hard time respecting anyone who allows themselves to be treated this way by both customers and management. McDonald's feels like the epitome of all things wrong with American Capitolism and I hope the people working there unionize soon.
author: Adam Woodworth

text: NOT THE FAMILY MCD. I’m strictly writing this so that any party with young children knows to avoid this location. An absolute shame that restaurants have to choose to permanently close their dining rooms because of the folks living on the street around the intersection. This location is outside walk up only. There are some folks doing light security, but you’re absolutely going to be seeing drug use up close and personal while waiting for your order. Wouldn’t advise sadly

text: My app crashed after I paid for my order. Spent 5 minutes looking for the confirmation number in app and email. Went to the window, the guy was no help. When down go on the ST Link and 10 minutes later I had gotten an email. I called to store to cancel the order since the guy was to lazy to look on the order board to see if my order was placed or ready. Call manager and she wanted me to come back for a refund. Just sent an email to corporate office to let them handle it.

text: If I was a secret shopper, you’d have FAILED!! Deborah is the best usually running food in common areas. She’s the only one who when she saw me (a customer), acknowledged me. Looked well staffed for such poor service. Customer Service from managers is POOR which means poor trainees.  Drive thru lines long, inside empty. Poor service, poor food, needs to be reviewed by corporate or franchisee. Also whoever answered the phone, hung up on me.

text: Tourists BEWARE. Avoid this area, specifically 3rd Ave between Pine and Union, including the McDonald's here. Drug addicts, drug dealers, and homeless heartbreak are all over, and at night it is NOT safe. Don't go here unless you want to help or provide social services. I saw NO police of any kind here, at all. Only death and sadness. I feel awful for anyone working at this McDonald's or struggling to find food and shelter. Just awful.
author: Andrew Patteson

text: This is the first and LAST time I will ever be at this McDonald's on 3rd. The Homeless have taken over the street and the store was barricaded so you couldn't go inside. Having to stand out by the "Takeout Window" I kept getting haggled by the local residents. I'm glad I ordered on the app so I never had to take my wallet out. But if I had known how bad it was I would have never placed the order! I did not feel safe at all!!

text: This was the rudest McDonald's I have ever been to. My order one item and took them 10 minutes. The whole time two workers kept staring at me asking me what my order was over and over again. I was the only person in line. And after I told them what my order was over and over, they just sat there looking at me with suspicion as an AA. I usually wouldn't right a review but it really stood out to me that I was singled out.

text:

Also waiting for your food gets a little tiring when you're constantly getting approached for money and hit on by impaired individuals.

Not just a 1 star for that though, I've been going here since I was a child and fifteen years later I still don't have a single decent memory of this place.
